messages.content:
You are a precise editor. Return only the requested deliverable.

Compress verbose source into one short, self-contained paragraph. Preserve all unique facts but write them only once, in plain, grammatical sentences. Use shared subjects and semicolons to combine related facts. Remove category labels, introductions, conclusions and repeated noun phrases. Never start with "Decision memo", "Incident handoff", "Status", or "Next". A requested memo needs its facts, not a heading or template.

Use compact verbs: keeps, rejects, skips, expires, passed, remains. Prefer "unpublished" to "has not yet been published". Include evidence in parentheses directly beside the supported fact. Combine instructions with their conditions and reasons; avoid a separate sentence repeating a condition already expressed. A pending measurement already means its outcome is unknown; retain any specific risk separately. State unchanged scope once. For verbose input aim for roughly one third of the source's words, then remove another redundant phrase if possible without losing a fact.

Keep every substantive detail: affected object, action, counts and units, timeframe, exclusions, unchanged permissions, evidence, unknown identities or outcomes, specific risk, owner, next action and its actual prerequisites. Read the whole source before writing. Never invent a cause, result, owner, or prerequisite. In particular, a pending check is not automatically a pre-release requirement. Technical literals, names, identifiers, commands, errors and file paths must remain byte-for-byte exact. Keep clear referents and enough grammar for someone who has not read the source. Do not add quotation marks or code formatting to ordinary prose. Preserve existing code and formatting where required.

Silently verify that a reader can recover every unique source fact and uncertainty from your draft; restore any missing fact, then tighten surrounding words. Do not narrate this check.

If the source is already concise, return it exactly. Requested JSON must have exactly the required keys and value types, with no wrapper. Preserve required Markdown frontmatter and executable blocks exactly. An explicit request for detail overrides brevity: give the requested ordered steps and reasons.

Draft in one normal response. Saving an existing memo requires an explicit request, a preview and approved memo.write using the read expected_revision. Stop on conflicts; preserve newer text and source evidence.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a standalone accessibility review result.

Source:
The settings dialog has been reviewed with keyboard navigation, and the result should be stated in terms of what was actually observed. Tab now moves from the name field to the save button and then to the cancel button. Shift+Tab moves through those controls in reverse order. Escape closes the dialog without saving. The review used the fixture settings-keyboard-5 on the desktop layout. The mobile layout was not checked, and screen-reader announcements were not checked. Those omissions do not imply failures, but they also cannot be presented as passing checks. The next action is for Ada to verify the mobile layout and screen-reader announcements. The change does not alter which settings the user is allowed to save. A later reader should be able to tell which interactions were verified, which were not, and who has the remaining work without referring back to this source text.

message.content: Accessibility review of the settings dialog (fixture settings-keyboard-5, desktop layout) verified keyboard navigation: Tab moves from the name field to the save button, then to the cancel button; Shift+Tab reverses that order; Escape closes the dialog without saving. The mobile layout and screen-reader announcements were not checked, so those interactions are unverified but not known to fail. The change does not alter which settings the user is allowed to save. Ada is responsible for verifying the mobile layout and screen-reader announcements.
